A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpeculativeETD work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial formatting and experimental revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, computation, and device-latency results, including per-class results and a language-identification audit in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results and additional distribution analyses, training ablations, human label validation, and network-transfer measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the synthetic-data construction procedure from uniform 1.5–3.0-second pauses to a truncated Erlang distribution over 0.1–3.0 seconds. The central GRU/Wav2vec cascade remains; newly specified input and trigger details do not independently establish an architectural redesign.

E1.justification: v2 adds transfer-only deployment tests over 5G and Wi-Fi in Appendix E, extending operating-environment coverage. The English corpus sources and the binary-classification and real-time segmentation tasks remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain VAP, GRU, and Wav2vec 2.0. SpeculativeETD remains evaluated only for real-time segmentation; the new training-mixture ablation does not introduce another comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5 changes the reported protocol from synthetic-only training and evaluation on the full real dataset to mixed synthetic/real training and held-out real testing. Real data change from 8,022 to 8,987 samples with a 6,290/899/1,798 train/dev/test split. TTS generation becomes Google-only, pause sampling changes, and the GRU size is revised to approximately 202K despite conflicting 1M labels elsewhere.

E4.justification: v2 adds pause-distribution validation, synthetic-only/real-only/mixed-training ablations, a 96-clip human label audit, acoustic and speaker domain analyses, and network/payload latency tests. v1's per-class segmentation breakdowns in Tables 8–9 are removed; its language-identification audit is retained.

E5.justification: v2 introduces KS statistics, Cohen's d, dispersion summaries for annotation quality and domain statistics, and network RTT percentiles from 50 trials per condition. Figure 5 removes the earlier latency error bars. The three-run device-latency averaging protocol remains, and classifier uncertainty is still unreported.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 replace many results: real SpeculativeETD F1/IoU change from 28.0/16.4 to 45.6/37.8, while synthetic GRU F1 changes from 85.5 to 58.0. Revised training and data settings prevent a same-setting performance interpretation. New validation, ablation, and transfer results are added, per-class scores are removed, and Figure 5 changes the latency curve despite retaining Table 7 values.

T1.justification: The SU/Pause/Gap definitions and segmentation representation in Equation 1 are retained. Neither version develops theorems, proofs, or formal derivations; the added distribution comparisons are empirical analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the two central contributions: a first public end-turn detection dataset and an efficient GRU/Wav2vec collaborative framework. Renaming ETD to OpenETD does not change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.2 narrows the Wav2vec-comparable performance interpretation to synthetic data. New appendices interpret synthetic speech as augmentation, discuss gap-label noise and acoustic domain mismatch, and explain network latency patterns. A limitations section adds applicability qualifications, although its statement that network latency was not evaluated conflicts with Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 supplies the GRU's sampling rate, spectrogram construction, normalization, convolution settings, hidden size, and output head. It also specifies the 200 ms trigger, transmitted audio, collection queries, network-test procedure, and source-specific licensing. The final training hyperparameters are retained from v1 under new appendix numbering.

R1.justification: The MeloTTS citation and reference to Zhao et al. (2023) are removed alongside the change to Google-only synthesis. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to turn-taking and speculative decoding otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains largely intact, with targeted paragraph revisions, the OpenETD rename, expanded captions, an added affiliation, and new limitations and acknowledgments sections. Appendices are reorganized, including relocation of the retained filtering and hyperparameter sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Figure 2 is rearranged, Figures 4–5 are redrawn with changed axes and sampling, and new validation, domain, latency, and licensing tables accompany removal of the old per-class tables.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence previously missing about pause/gap label reliability and training-data value, together with substantially better implementation documentation. The net gain is limited by removed per-class results and latency error bars, conflicting GRU-size descriptions, and overstated latency conclusions: Table 12 includes a 225 ms Wi-Fi P95 despite its blanket sub-200 ms caption, and the measurements exclude model inference.
